subject: gunblade
pitch:
Category: Weapon.
Subject: gunblade.
Style: Final Fantasy.

spec.name: Gunblade — Lionheart Revolver
spec.description: A Final Fantasy-style gunblade standing upright on its pommel: a revolver mechanism fused to a greatsword, barrel running along the blade's spine to a muzzle at the tip, brass filigree and a glowing cyan magic stone.
spec.layout: The weapon stands bolt upright on its pommel at the origin, fully vertical, model front (+Z) is the blade's cutting-edge side, back (−Z) is the spine where the barrel runs. From the floor upward: brass-capped pommel with a red gem at y 0-0.1; the leather-wrapped grip tapering up to y 0.62 with a brass trigger guard loop facing +Z and a steel trigger inside it; the revolver mechanism block y 0.62-1.02 with a six-flute dark drum at its centre, a brass stud ring, a top strap bridging over the drum and a hammer cocked back at −Z; the crossguard with wing-like quillons and a glowing cyan crystal seated where blade meets mechanism at y ~1.05; the greatsword blade slab rising to y 2.18, widest at the ricasso and sweeping to a spear tip, its polished cutting edge facing +Z, a dark fuller groove running up the flats, a brass heraldic wing emblem engraved on both sides near the base and a column of rune studs marching up one flat; the octagonal gunmetal barrel clamped to the blade's spine (−Z side) by two brass bands, terminating in a ringed muzzle brake and front sight just below the tip. Style everywhere: cold faceted low-poly steel with hard black seams, warm brass fittings with rivets and engraved trim, dark oiled leather on the grip, one strong cyan magic glow at the guard crystal and a fainter glow down the muzzle bore.

parts.builds: The lower hilt standing on the floor. Pommel: a small turned dome (lathe) of brass with a dark steelLow collar under it and a faceted ruby cabochon set in its cap, its lowest point touching y=0. Grip body: a tapered octagonal prism (frustumBox or sweep with 8 sides) in gripWood from y 0.08 to 0.6, leaning a hair toward −Z so the weapon balances over the drum. Leather wrap: 4 broad diagonal straps (thin swept bands or slabs) of leather wrapping the grip at a spiral, each edged with a hairline of leatherDark, and 3 brass band stitches crossing them. Trigger guard: a flat brass loop (swept arc or extruded band, ~8 mm thick) bulging forward (+Z) from the grip front down to the guard bow, with a small brass rivet at each end. Trigger: a slender curved steelMid blade hanging inside the guard on the trigger joint, with an ink outline sliver. Lanyard: a small brass ring on the pommel's left side (+X) with a 4-link dark chain and a short leather tassel hanging free but never touching the floor (ends above y=0.02). Every piece rides the weapon joint except the trigger, which rides the trigger joint.
parts.attaches: Pommel bottom rests on y=0 (floor part). Grip top end caps onto the mechanism's frame at mount gripTop [0, 0.62, 0]; the trigger hinge sits inside the guard bow.

parts.builds: The revolver action block between grip and blade. Drum: a six-flute cylinder (lathe with 6 flat segments, radius 0.13, axis vertical) in gunmetal riding the drum joint, each flute face wearing an ink seam line, with a ring of 6 small brass bolt heads around its top face and a steelLight ejector star on its centre cap. Frame: a gunmetal housing (loft or frustumBox pair) that wraps the drum from the grip top up to drumTop, with steelDark side plates on both flats (±X), each plate carrying a panel of brass inlay lines and 4 rivets. Top strap: a steelMid bridge arching over the drum front-to-back with an ink slot and a brass screw at each end. Hammer: a steelDark spur cocked back over the −Z side at the top of the frame, pivoting visually on a brass pin, with a steelLight notch on its face. Loading gate: a small hinged brass plate on the frame's right flat (−X) with a knurled thumb piece. Barrel breech: a short stout steelDark collar at the frame's top-centre where the barrel will slot in, facing up. Everything rides the weapon joint except the drum itself.
parts.attaches: Frame bottom sockets down over mount gripTop [0, 0.62, 0]; frame top hands off to blade and fittings at mount drumTop [0, 1.02, 0]; the barrel breech collar meets the barrel part at mount barrelRoot [0, 1.06, -0.1].

parts.builds: The greatsword blade. Main slab: an extruded blade silhouette (wide ricasso ~0.24 m across at the base in Z, gentle forward curve, sweeping to a spear point at y 2.18) built along +Y with its thickness along X (thickness tapering 0.05 to 0.02, bevelled), faceted in steelMid. Cutting edge: a polished edgePolished strip (thin extrude or swept bevel) running the full +Z face of the blade from ricasso to tip. Fuller: a recessed groove (a slim ink-topped steelDark inset slab) running up the centre of each flat from y 1.1 to y 1.7. Ricasso etch: a brass heraldic wing emblem built from 6-10 small angled slabs and a round brass boss, mirrored on both flats at y ~1.2. Runes: a column of 7 small glowing cyan rune studs (tiny extruded glyphs) marching up the +X flat from y 1.3 to 1.9. Spine cap: a steelLight strip along the blade's −Z spine that the barrel sits against, with an ink seam under it. Tip facet: the last 0.15 m of the blade split into two steelLight chamfer faces meeting the polished edge, so the point reads bright. All rides the weapon joint.
parts.attaches: Blade base seats down onto mount drumTop [0, 1.02, 0] inside the crossguard's ring; the spine strip (−Z face of the box) receives the barrel part along mount barrelRoot [0, 1.06, -0.1]; the crossguard from fittings wraps this box at mount guardPlane.

parts.builds: The gun barrel along the blade's back. Barrel body: an octagonal tube (sweep with 8 sides or stacked frustumBoxes) in gunmetal, radius ~0.045, running from the mechanism's breech at y 1.06 straight up to y 2.02, hugging the blade's spine at z ≈ −0.13, with 2 thin ink cooling-ring seams along its length. Muzzle: a brass reinforcing ring at the top, then a short steelDark crown cylinder with a recessed bore whose inner face is a glowing cyan disc (glow at strength 1) so the bore reads lit; a small steelLight front-sight blade rises from the ring toward the sword tip. Barrel bands: 2 brass clamp bands (short swept loops) wrapping barrel and spine strip together at y ~1.35 and y ~1.7, each with 3 rivet heads and an ink shadow line under the band. Rear sight: a tiny notched steelLight leaf on the first band. All rides the weapon joint.
parts.attaches: Barrel root slots into the mechanism's breech collar at mount barrelRoot [0, 1.06, -0.1] and its bands clamp onto the spine strip of the bladeCore box; its muzzle stops just below the blade tip.

parts.builds: The crossguard and magic furniture at the blade base. Crossguard: a broad swept brass plate (extrude or slab pair) wrapping the blade's base at y 1.02-1.12, flaring out ±X into two upturned wing-shaped quillons whose tips curl toward +Z, each wing edged with brassDark trim and 3 rivets, with an ink shadow line where it meets the drum top. Gem mount: at the guard's front-centre a brass rosette cradling a faceted cyan crystal (octahedron or low-seg lathe), glowing bright (glowCyan, glow strength 1.4) with a glowCore inner core part. Filigree: 4 slender brassDark filigree strips and 2 small wing fins laid on the guard's top face. Chains: two short 3-link dark chains (steelDark links) drooping from the guard's left and right quillon roots back to the mechanism's frame side plates, hanging within this box. Side plates: 2 small steelLight shoulder plates seating against the drum top, riveted in brass. All rides the weapon joint.
parts.attaches: Guard ring seats down onto mount drumTop [0, 1.02, 0] around the bladeCore base and against the mechanism's frame top; chain upper ends meet the mechanism frame's side plates, lower ends anchor at the quillon roots at mount guardPlane [0, 1.06, 0].

Classic FF8 gunblade: revolver cylinder at hilt, barrel along the back edge (spine) of the blade, muzzle where the blade tip begins, revolver grip.

Plan: display the weapon standing upright, point down? Or laid at an angle? Better: standing vertically, grip at bottom resting on floor like planted? Or displayed angled. Simplest readable: the gunblade planted into ground? Weapons typically: standing on tip, leaning. Or rest horizontally on a display stand? The brief says "the subject is the whole deliverable; ground, rocks, props or scenery appear only where the brief names them". Brief doesn't name a stand, so no scenery. So the weapon itself must rest on y=0. A gunblade standing on its pommel/grip bottom, blade pointing up and slightly forward, is dramatic and reads well.

Size: gunblades are large. Let's do total height ~2.2 m (oversized JRPG sword). Width ~0.5 m, length (z) ~0.6 m for grip protrusion. Layout: grip at bottom (y 0–0.55), revolver cylinder at y ~0.55–0.85, guard/trigger, then blade rising up to y ~2.1 with muzzle near the base of the blade... Let me include root joint `bladeRoot` role... roles list: spine neck head jaw hinge tail leg arm wing digit tentacle fan. For a weapon, hinge joints could be useful: trigger, cylinder (drum). Let's add: root "weapon" at grip base role "spine"; "trigger" hinge; "drum" hinge (revolving cylinder could spin); "boltAction"? Keep modest: weapon (root, spine), drum (hinge), trigger (hinge). Parts list these.

1. gripHilt — grip, pommel, trigger guard, trigger, grip wrap details. box: y 0–0.6.
2. revolverCore — drum/cylinder, frame, hammer, trigger housing, barrel breech, mounts to grip top. y 0.55–1.0.
